hardinessNote: Hardy in most places throughout the UK, approximately -15 to -10°C.
visual: Lacy white blooms turn rose then deep pink · exceptionally compact · long flowering
water: Water regularly, especially in sun and containers; do not allow the rootball to dry out.
prune: In spring cut last year's stems back to a pair of healthy buds.
toxicity: Plant material is harmful if eaten and may cause stomach upset; dogs and cats are at risk. Handling may trigger skin allergy, so wear gloves.
compliance: PBR protected: 'Breg14', CPVO EU52722; commercial propagation requires permission. UK plant passport rules apply to professional movement.
cvs: This plant: 'Breg14' = (S)WITCH 'Ophelia' / POLESTAR · 'Little Lime' – compact green-white · 'Limelight' – larger lime-white panicles
resilience: Hardy and reliable; may get aphids, capsid bug, hydrangea scale, vine weevil, leaf spot, mildew or Botrytis.
uses: Patio containers · small gardens · front of borders · courtyards · cut flowers
foliage: deciduous; broadly oval, coarsely toothed green leaves
uncertain: Flowering is variously described as roughly June-September, June-October and June-November; Jun-Oct is used for a practical UK display season.
Breeder material claims substantially lower temperature tolerance than the RHS H5 rating; RHS H5 is retained for UK card consistency.
Published root depth and spread data specific to 'Breg14' were not found, so rootSize is blank.
sources: Breederplants – Hydrangea paniculata Breg14 (Polestar) PBR EU52722
DEFRA / UK Plant Health Information Portal – UK Plant Passport guidance

hardinessNote: Hardy in most places throughout the UK, approximately -15 to -10°C.
visual: Double pompon daisies in pink, red or white · compact rosettes · spring colour
water: Keep evenly moist; water containers when the surface begins to dry.
prune: Deadhead to prolong flowering; cut back after flowering.
toxicity: Edible petals are used as garnish, but eating large amounts of the plant may cause stomach upset; children and pets should not eat nursery-grown bedding plants.
cvs: 'Tasso' – compact pompon flowers · 'Pomponette' – small quilled doubles · Bellissima Series – larger double pompons
resilience: Generally pest-free; rust can occur; established plants tolerate cold conditions well.
uses: Autumn and spring bedding · edging · containers · window boxes
foliage: evergreen; compact rosettes of spoon-shaped dark green leaves
uncertain: Exact cultivar or series was unreadable, so this record is deliberately generic at Bellis perennis species level for double bedding forms.
hue is null because commercial double Bellis are sold in pink, red and white and the exact colour is unknown.
Hardiness varies by commercial series: RHS lists Tasso at H5, Pomponette at H6 and some Bellis forms at H7; H5 is used conservatively for an unidentified bedding form.
Height and spread are representative of compact double bedding forms because the exact series is unknown.
Toxicity evidence is inconsistent: RHS lists Bellis perennis petals as edible, while some other horticultural references report gastrointestinal effects after larger ingestion.
